newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK STRINTZIS SEES 96 PROFITS UP 19PCT.
newsitem.headline: GREEK STRINTZIS SEES 96 PROFITS UP 19PCT.

text.p: Greek shipper Strintzis Lines expects profits to rise 19 percent to 2.5 billion drachmas in 1996, a company financial executive told Reuters.
"We are expecting final figures at the end of this week, but we have some estimates for higher profits, sales and dividends in 1996," he said.
Profits are estimated 2.5 billion drachmas in 1996, up 19 percent on 1995 from 2.1 billion in 1995.
Strintzis forecasted sales of 21.5 billion drachmas in 1996 from 18.2 billion in 1995 in an earlier statement.
Dividend per share is expected to be higher than 60 drachmas in 1995.
Strintzis Lines sold its passenger ship Delos to foreign buyers at a price higher than book value, it said in a statement on Monday.
The company has asked the merchant marine ministry for a license to replace Delos with another ship covering the same route as well as licenses for two new ships to serve internal routes.
